newsitem.title: GERMANY: Autopsy shows German woman's death not BSE-related.
newsitem.headline: Autopsy shows German woman's death not BSE-related.

text.p: German health authorities said on Saturday that a woman who died last month was not Germany's first victim of the human equivalent of mad cow disease.

Authorities in the Schleswig-Holstein state where she died said an autopsy showed the cause of death was the classic form of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), not a suspected new strain which scientists believe may be linked to mad cow disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE).

The woman's relative youth, 41, had indicated she may have been a victim of the new, fast-acting CJD strain which scientists say claims young victims -- unlike the classic strain that affects the elderly.
Authorities had obtained her relatives' permission to perform the autopsy -- the only way of confirming the presence of the brain-wasting disease.
"The thorough examination by neuropaths showed that the woman died of the classic form of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease," the state's health ministry said in a statement.
"According to our experts the so-called new strain of the disease can definitely be ruled out."

The case had added to German consumers' worries about beef from Britain, which has had over 165,000 cases of BSE and where several people have died from what is believed to be the new BSE-related CJD.
